title: Ingress circuit breaker sketchbook
content:
Personal scratchpad for an ingress-side circuit breaker + soft-degradation policy. Meant as a lightweight alternative to heavy per-route throttles; designed to be compatible with Redwood routing and fallback model-variant behavior. Notes, examples, questions, and a tiny ascii diagram below.

Goals / constraints:
- fast decision at edge proxy (kubed ingress / envoy / edge-proxy) with small per-connection state
- support multi-tenant per-route SLOs and global capacity signals
- graceful fallback to cheaper/compatible model variants when capacity constrained
- allow operators to opt into automatic half-open recovery or manual override

Key concepts (quick):
- CircuitBreakerConfig: per-route policy (tenant, route-id, model-group) controlling thresholds and backoff
- Local short-term counters: sliding window success/latency/error counts (millisecond granularity)
- Global capacity signal: from scheduler/allocator (REST / push) indicates "pressure level" (0-100) per pool
- Backpressure actions: slow-path queueing, immediate 429, fallback to variant, or buffered async response
- Telemetry: trace tags + histograms for decision reason, exposure time, and fallback delta

Proposed API shape (flat JSON-ish for config storage):
- CircuitBreakerConfig (persisted in config store):
  id: string (route-id or generated)
  scope: ["tenant:ID", "global", "route:NAME"]
  sample_window_ms: int (e.g. 1000)
  min_requests_for_eval: int (e.g. 20)
  error_rate_threshold: float (0.0-1.0) // percent errors to open
  p99_latency_ms_threshold: int // if exceeded opens
  open_backoff_ms: int // base backoff when open
  max_backoff_ms: int
  half_open_probe_count: int // concurrent probes allowed when half-open
  fallback_mode: ["none", "model_variant", "queue", "reject"]
  fallback_variant: string|null // model id
  capacity_signal_weight: float (0.0-1.0) // weight to blend global capacity into open probability

Example config (single-line JSON):
{"id":"route-accounts-search","scope":"route:accounts-search","sample_window_ms":1000,"min_requests_for_eval":30,"error_rate_threshold":0.12,"p99_latency_ms_threshold":600,"open_backoff_ms":2000,"max_backoff_ms":30000,"half_open_probe_count":3,"fallback_mode":"model_variant","fallback_variant":"gptq-7b-qa","capacity_signal_weight":0.4}

Decision function (sketch):
- maintain circular buffer of per-request records: {ts, latency_ms, status_code, decision}
- every sample_window_ms, compute error_rate, p99_latency; if requests >= min_requests_for_eval then compute open_score = alpha * normalized_error + beta * normalized_latency + gamma * (1 - capacity_signal)
- if open_score > threshold -> transition to OPEN and set next_reopen_time = now + open_backoff_ms * backoff_multiplier (capped at max_backoff)
- OPEN: apply fallback_mode until next_reopen_time
- HALF_OPEN: allow half_open_probe_count requests to try primary; if success ratio > pass_threshold -> CLOSE else increase backoff

Pseudocode (very rough):
function evaluate(window, capacity_signal) {
  normalized_error = window.error_rate // 0..1
  normalized_latency = min(1, window.p99 / config.p99_latency_ms_threshold)
  open_score = (1-config.capacity_signal_weight) * (w1*normalized_error + w2*normalized_latency) + config.capacity_signal_weight * (1 - capacity_signal)
  return open_score
}

Operations / state storage:
- keep per-route ephemeral state in edge-proxy memory (LRU for low-traffic routes)
- persist CircuitBreakerConfig in config service + push to proxies via config-stream
- backoff multiplier remembered per-route (ex: exp backoff 2^n)
- twin telemetry counters sent to Console (cb_reason, cb_state, cb_open_duration_ms, fallback_used)

Integration with Redwood features:
- fallback to model_variant -> Redwood routing should accept variant override header (x-redwood-variant) to route to quantized or cheaper pool
- capacity_signal: aggregator in platform (sre/orchestration) publishes per-pool pressure. Edge can subscribe with small envelope.
- tracing: include cb_decision and cb_score as span attributes for evals

ASCII diagram (super tiny):
client -> edge-proxy -> routing-layer -> (primary pool)
                      |               
                      +-> fallback pool (variant)
                      |               
                      +-> queue / delayed response

Open questions / TODOs (for followups):
- metricizing p99 vs tail-latency on short windows: p99 on 1s windows is noisy for low QPS; consider iqr or burst detector
- how much weight to give capacity_signal? ops wants aggressive fallback when capacity>0.8 but product worried about quality
- should we include per-tenant budgets so a tenant can never be fully rejected by global pressure? (tenant priority)
- integration tests: create chaos test that floods route and verify fallback variant invoked and CircuitBreaker metrics appear
- edge memory budget: design an LRU eviction policy for route state older than 5m
- operator manual override: UI switch in Console to force OPEN / CLOSE per-route

Notes to self (style / UX):
- keep decisions explainable in the UI: show the contributing factors (error component, latency component, capacity component)
- prefer "soft" strategies (route to cheaper variant) over hard rejects wherever possible for PLG customers

Links / references in my head:
- INF-2382 (P0 research ticket for ingress backpressure)
- prior notes: latency-simulator-load-profile-notebook.json and pref/defaults experiments
- existing fallback header RFC (search for x-redwood-variant)

Micro-experiments to run (next week):
- simulate poisson traffic with injected errors and measure cb open/close frequency for candidate alpha/beta values
- test quantized fallback quality delta on 100 prompt set and measure user-visible regression

End of scratchbook. This is pretty rough — mostly for me to share with Ravi and Lucia tomorrow.

Maya
